intro: DNP3 is how many electric and water utilities, mostly in North America and Australia, connect SCADA (the control room's supervisory system) to their outstations: the devices out in the field, such as RTUs (remote terminal units, which collect a site's signals), relays and reclosers. Every point (signal) has a type and an index, its number. The outstation keeps each change as an event, with its time, until the master, SCADA, confirms it has it. It can also send events unasked, as soon as they happen.
plain: DNP3 lets a utility's control room keep watch over equipment spread across a power or water network. Each site writes down every change with its exact time, like a logbook. It reports the changes, by itself or when asked. It crosses them off only when the control room says "got it", like a parcel signed for on delivery, so no change is lost even if a message goes missing.

connect.title: Open the connection
connect.text: SCADA opens a TCP connection (a reliable link between two computers) to the RTU on port 20000. DNP3 has its own addresses too: SCADA is master 1, the RTU is outstation 10.

poll.title: Read everything
poll.text: SCADA sends an integrity poll: a read of everything. It asks for class 1, 2 and 3 (the events: changes waiting to be reported) and class 0 (the current value of every point). There are no events yet, so the answer holds only current values.

enable.title: Allow unasked reports
enable.text: SCADA now lets the RTU send events without being asked. Such messages are called unsolicited responses. The RTU answers with an empty response.

trip.title: A breaker trips
trip.text: A fault hits the feeder, the line leaving the substation. The relay that protects it trips (opens) breaker CB-1 and tells the RTU. 50 ms later the breaker is open. The RTU stamps each change with its time, keeps both in its event buffer (its list of changes not yet confirmed) and sends them at once.

confirm.title: Confirm receipt
confirm.text: SCADA confirms that it got both events. Only now does the RTU delete them from its buffer. Without the confirmation, it would send them again.

frames.tcp: Open a TCP connection to port 20000
frames.read: Send me all events and every current value
frames.response: CB-1 closed, no trip, bus at 11050 V
frames.enable: You may send events by yourself now
frames.unsolicited: Trip at .230, CB-1 open at .280. Please confirm

notes.tcp: Plain TCP from 10.0.0.10 to 10.0.0.20, port 20000. Even over TCP, every DNP3 message then travels in a DNP3 link frame, with its CRCs (error checks).
notes.relay-contact: A wire, not DNP3: the relay's trip output also closes a contact on binary input 1 (an on/off input) of the RTU. The RTU notes the time: 10:41:07.230.
notes.aux-contact: A wire too: the breaker's auxiliary contact, a switch that moves with the breaker, tells binary input 0 that CB-1 is open, at 10:41:07.280.

start.name: Start
start.note: Every DNP3 link frame starts with 0x0564.

len-20.name: Length 20
len-20.note: The bytes from the control field to the end of the data, CRCs not counted: 5 of header, 15 of data.

ctrl-master.name: Link control
ctrl-master.note: 0xC4: from the master (DIR 1), starting a transfer (PRM 1, primary), function 4: user data that needs no link-layer confirmation.

ctrl-out.name: Link control
ctrl-out.note: 0x44: from the outstation (DIR 0), primary, function 4: user data that needs no link-layer confirmation.

dest-10.name: Destination 10
dest-10.note: The outstation's address, 2 bytes, low byte first.

crc-head.name: CRC
crc-head.note: An error check over the 8 header bytes before it. CRC-16/DNP, low byte first.

crc-block.name: CRC
crc-block.note: Checks the data block before it. Data travels in blocks of up to 16 bytes, each with its own CRC.

crc-split.name: CRC
crc-split.note: Checks the first 16 data bytes. It falls between the start and the stop index: blocks are cut every 16 bytes, whatever the bytes mean.

crc-split-time.name: CRC
crc-split-time.note: Checks the first 16 data bytes. It cuts the first time stamp in two: its last byte comes after the CRC.

th-0.name: Transport
th-0.note: 0xC0: FIR and FIN are both set, so this segment is the first and the last: the message fits in one. Sequence 0. Each side counts its own segments.

ac-read.name: App control
ac-read.note: 0xC2: FIR and FIN, a request in one fragment, sequence 2.

ac-response.name: App control
ac-response.note: 0xC2: sequence 2, the same as the request: this is its answer. CON 0: there are no events in it, so no confirmation is needed.

ac-uns.name: App control
ac-uns.note: 0xF0: CON 1 (confirm this) and UNS 1 (unsolicited: nobody asked), sequence 0. Unsolicited messages have their own sequence numbers.

ac-confirm.name: App control
ac-confirm.note: 0xD0: UNS 1, sequence 0: this confirms unsolicited message 0.

fc-response.name: Function 0x81
fc-response.note: RESPONSE: the answer to a request.

fc-enable.name: Function 0x14
fc-enable.note: 20: ENABLE_UNSOLICITED, for the classes that follow.

iin.name: IIN
iin.note: Internal indications: 16 status bits. All 0: no events waiting, no trouble, the clock is set.

class1.name: g60v2
class1.note: Group 60, variation 2: class 1 events. Qualifier 0x06: all of them.

class0.name: g60v1
class0.note: Class 0: the current value of every point.

g1v2.name: g1v2
g1v2.note: Group 1, variation 2: binary inputs (on/off signals), one flags byte each.

q00.name: Qualifier 0x00
q00.note: A range follows: a 1-byte start index and a 1-byte stop index.

bi0-closed.name: BI 0
bi0-closed.note: 0x81: online (bit 0) and state 1 (bit 7): CB-1 is closed.

g30v2.name: g30v2
g30v2.note: Group 30, variation 2: analog inputs (measured values), 16 bits, with flags.

stop-0.name: Stop 0
stop-0.note: … and stops at index 0: one point.

ai0.name: AI 0
ai0.note: 0x2B2A = 11050, low byte first: the bus voltage, in volts.

g2v2.name: g2v2
g2v2.note: Group 2, variation 2: binary input events, each with its absolute time.

q17.name: Qualifier 0x17
q17.note: A 1-byte count, then a 1-byte index before each object.

t-trip.name: Time
t-trip.note: Milliseconds since 1970 in 6 bytes, low byte first: 2026-11-12 10:41:07.230 UTC. The sixth byte comes after the CRC.

t-trip-end.name: Time, last byte
t-trip-end.note: The sixth byte of the time stamp.

a-fin.name: FIN
a-fin.note: Final fragment. With FIR set too, the message fits in one fragment.

a-con.name: CON
a-con.note: Confirmation requested. The outstation sets it when the message holds events, so that it knows when it may delete them.

a-uns.name: UNS
a-uns.note: Unsolicited: nobody asked for this message.

a-seq.name: SEQ 0
a-seq.note: Sequence number, 0 to 15. The confirmation must carry the same one.

facts.frames: Link frame with CRCs → transport segment → application fragment

tips: Each frame carries two DNP3 addresses, master 1 and outstation 10 here. Both are settings. A frame to the wrong address is dropped silently, with no error.
Events wait in the outstation until the master confirms them. If the buffer fills up, the oldest are lost and IIN2.3 (event buffer overflow) is set. Poll and confirm often enough.
IIN1.4 (need time) means the outstation's clock is not set. Until someone sets it, its event times are wrong.
A firewall can close a quiet TCP connection without either side noticing. Turn on the keep-alive: a link status request (05 64 05 C9 …) when nothing has arrived for a while.

playground.file: The RTU's DNP3 settings and point list. SCADA needs the same addresses, and the same idea of what each index means.
playground.addresses: The outstation's own address, then the master it answers. They must match the link headers.
playground.keepalive: After 60 s without traffic, send a link status request to find a dead connection.
playground.unsol-classes: The event classes that may go out unsolicited, once the master enables them.
playground.confirm-timeout: How long to wait for a confirmation before sending the events again.
playground.buffer: How many events of each kind the RTU keeps. When it is full, the oldest are lost.

playground.event: How its changes are sent: g2v2, with absolute time.
playground.class: Class 1: IIN1.1 shows when its events are waiting.
playground.analog-event: g32v4: a 16-bit analog input event with time.
playground.deadband: A new analog event is made only when the value moves by more than 50 V.

timing.title: Asked every 10 s, or told at once
timing.note: SCADA reads the outstation's events every 10 s here. Without unsolicited responses, a trip at 23 s would wait for the poll at 30 s. With them, the RTU sends it at once, and keeps the events until SCADA confirms; without the confirm, it sends them again.
